setting: The drowned coast, around 2140, where the seas took the old cities and people live on lashed-together rafts and salvaged boats, diving the flooded towers for anything worth trading to buy a place up on the high ground. Life is cold, close, and loud, and every good seat is above the waterline. Below a certain depth in the towers, people start losing memory, and it never comes back.
heart: This is about people who go down into the dark for each other and surface missing pieces of themselves, and about whether loving someone means telling them the truth about who they've become. What's at stake is a body, a home, and the memory of the people you'd die to save.

cast.name: Sol Ferreira
cast.role: captain of the salvage boat the Marrow
cast.wants: enough money to buy her crew berths on the highland arcology before storm season drowns their mooring
cast.flaw: hides how much of her memory she's already lost and won't hand anyone the helm.
cast.status: at the drum on the manual ratchet, calling depth, one pull left

cast.name: Dey Okafor
cast.role: newest diver, indentured to the crew
cast.wants: one big score to buy back his freedom
cast.flaw: dives too deep to prove himself and won't call for help until it's far too late.
cast.status: unconscious on deck, gray-lipped, missing his last hour, slate empty below thirty meters

cast.name: Wren Achebe
cast.role: the reader, the topside tech who rebuilds divers' lost hours from their slate recorders
cast.wants: to keep Dey from ending up hollowed out like Sol
cast.flaw: quietly edits the slates to spare people what they did, a lie she's built her whole job on.
cast.status: forty point five meters on the spliced line, past the line, twenty-two minutes down with nine she can't account for

cast.name: Nia Vos
cast.role: a girl surviving alone in the drowned hospital tower
cast.wants: to keep her little brother Teo alive on the last of his medicine
cast.flaw: trusts no one and has run the cold-box by hand for a year rather than ask for help, nearly dead herself.
cast.status: topside at the chart table, logging Wren's callouts in grease pencil

cast.name: Ivo Salas
cast.role: an old diver trapped in an air pocket at forty-two meters in the salvage tower
cast.wants: one ride up on the winch
cast.flaw: lends out the air he needs himself and trusts a stranger's promise
cast.status: two-way on the backup band at last, scrubber failing, saying Wren's name on request

cast.name: Anselm Rusk
cast.role: the Factor's collector, skipper of a barge that runs with no lights
cast.wants: to bring the Factor the cold-case's value or the Marrow itself before the storm turns, because his own berth rides on the debt he's owed
cast.flaw: certain every person has a price, so he keeps reading Sol's choice of the children over the money as a bluff he can call.
cast.status: cast off east into the rain on his lamp-less barge, returning at first light to take the case's value or the Marrow.

threads: Storm season will drown the Marrow’s mooring unless they buy berths on the high ground.
Why does the voice on the backup channel know Wren's name, which she never gave it?
Can the Marrow buy berths before the storm turns, with no money, no case, and Teo's medicine nearly gone?
The eleven-second cut in Wren's own record was made by her own hand last night, and she has no memory of making it or of the descent it erased.

arcs.title: Below the Line
arcs.goal: The Marrow takes a broker's fortune to raise a sealed medical cold-case from a drowned hospital tower, only to find the cargo is a girl and her dying brother, and must choose on their last air between the payout that would save the whole crew and two strangers. It ends with the strangers saved, the money gone, and a captain who no longer remembers what she gave up.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: The Line
plan.summary: On a routine dive Dey crosses the depth line and surfaces missing an hour, which Wren quietly rebuilds for him from his slate while Sol watches the storm glass and a broker's drone drops a contract to raise a cryo-case from the hospital tower for more money than they've ever seen.

plan.title: Too Good
plan.summary: Sol takes the Factor's contract over Wren's objection and loads extra oxygen, warning Dey as they descend that the deeper he goes the more of himself stays down there, but he pushes ahead to the case.

plan.title: The Air Pocket
plan.summary: In a flooded ward Dey finds the cryo-case guarded by Nia, who's kept it running a year to hold the medicine keeping her sick brother Teo alive, and begs them to leave — as Dey's memory starts coming apart from lingering too deep.

plan.title: The Choice
plan.summary: Dey slips badly and forgets the surface entirely, so Sol dives past her own limit to drag him up, sees the two kids running out of air, and over the radio chooses the people over the case.

plan.title: Empty-Handed
plan.summary: They surface into the storm with two children and no vault, Wren cuts off the Factor's drone as it demands the case, and Sol — down longest — comes up not remembering why her hands are empty.

plan.title: The Slate
plan.summary: Anchored in the storm with five mouths to feed and no berth money, Wren plays Sol's slate back to tell her what she chose, and her thumb finds the edit function she's used on everyone, hovering over the lie while Sol waits to hear who she saved.

chapterSummaries: Dey crossed the thirty-meter line on a routine locker dive and came up bent, missing the hour, carrying a name he shouldn't have — Ivo Salas, an old diver in an air pocket who lent him air. Wren spliced the name out of the build she played him; he kept it anyway. Sol can't read her own grease-pencil numbers. The Factor's drone dropped a contract: a sealed cold-case at fifty-two meters in the Mercy General, twelve thousand, a year of Dey's indenture retired, nine hours till the season is declared — and Wren's arithmetic says someone has hand-wound that cell for twenty-two years.

The Marrow ran six kilometers out to the Mercy General for the Factor's twelve-thousand cold-case, and Dey went down to fifty-two and came off the tether with his memory already going. He found the "cargo" is a girl hand-winding the case's power cell over a masked little boy, and she told him flat he isn't the man she's been waiting for — Ivo Salas — while Wren's thumb hovered over the slate.

In the flooded ward of the Mercy General, Dey's memory came apart until he sat down warm and empty against the cryo-case, forgetting the boat, "up," and why he came, while Nia cranked the failing spring cell one-handed over her brother Teo and the Factor's drone counted the crate and Wren could only talk to a man who'd stopped hearing her. Sol, watching her wax markers hang dead on the rail, pulled the spare full-face mask and told the boat she was going down herself.

At fifty-two meters in the Mercy General, Sol declared the cargo people and refused the Factor's count — forfeiting the twelve thousand and the crew's berths on the high ground — then crushed the underwater drone, sent Dey and the two children up on the drum's last powered pull, and stayed behind alone with ninety bar and no memory of the choice. Ivo Salas's call for the kid is still open and unanswered on the backup channel.

The Marrow came up into the storm with Nia and Teo but no cold-case; Wren jammed the Factor's drone over the side and hand-hauled Sol up the last cable through a snatch block with a dead winch. Teo's scrubber is spent, the berth money is gone, and Sol surfaced on ninety bar asking why her hands are empty. The whole unedited truth sits on her slate, Wren's thumb frozen over the edit.

Wren cued up Sol's slate to show her what she had given up, but Nia caught her thumb on the edit key. Wren cut the memory anyway, leaving Sol with only the warm half: three people hauled from the dark, no twelve thousand, no choice. Dey gave his scrubber cartridge to Teo so the boy could breathe, and the Factor's barge closed through the storm as Salas spoke Wren's name over the open channel.
arcs.summary: The Marrow raised a sealed cold-case from Mercy General and found Nia and Teo inside. Sol chose the children over the twelve-thousand payoff, crushing the Factor's drone and sending everyone up on the drum's last pull. They surfaced into the storm with no money, no berths, no case. Wren edited Sol's slate so she would not remember choosing them. Sol is peaceful but missing that hour; Dey gave his scrubber to Teo and can no longer dive safely; Nia carries the only true account; Salas still calls from forty-two meters knowing Wren's name.

arcs.title: The Pocket at Forty-Two Meters
arcs.goal: With one day before the storm and the Factor's collector, the Marrow's only score is a sealed pharmacy pocket at forty-two meters, guarded by a dying man who knows Wren's name; the arc ends with the medicine raised, the debt paid, and Wren giving Sol back the hour she cut.
arcs.author: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free

plan.title: No Running Lights
plan.summary: The lamp-less barge slides alongside and Rusk boards, gives Sol until the storm turns to hand over the cold-case's value or the Marrow itself, pockets Teo's spare medicine cartridges as earnest, and casts off remarking that the tower's picked clean except one flooded pocket at forty-two meters no diver has come back from.

plan.title: Eleven Seconds
plan.summary: Wren, who can't stop hearing her own name in Salas's call, runs a build on her own slate and finds the same eleven-second gap she cut from Sol's, and before anyone can stop him Dey rolls off the rail toward the tower on one breath with no scrubber to prove he still belongs in the deep.

plan.title: Below the Line
plan.summary: They haul Dey back hollowed and missing his last hour, so Sol takes the winch instead of the water and feeds Wren the last good air while she goes down the spliced line alone, and at forty-two meters Wren's lamp finds her own old knot still tied at the pocket.

plan.title: The Man Who Kept the Air
plan.summary: Salas, alive and shedding his year, tells Wren in pieces that he sealed two children in a Mercy General cold-case to float them clear and dove back for the boy's medicine before the tower took him, and that she came once and swore she'd bring the winch, then his scrubber hisses dry with the crates sitting just past him, deeper than her air can spare.

plan.title: What the Deep Keeps
plan.summary: Wren goes past the line to rig Salas and lash the medicine crates to the cable, Sol makes the drum's last good pull as the storm hits, and they surface with a living man, a fortune in medicine, and a Wren who doesn't remember why the girl on deck is crying.

plan.title: The Truth About Who You've Become
plan.summary: With Rusk back at the rail, Wren stops editing and gives Sol her real hour back, so Sol chooses the children again with her eyes open and pays Rusk off in medicine crates, keeping the boat, the berths, and the last of Teo's course, and when Salas wakes not knowing any of them and calls for someone to tell the kid to keep going, Wren for once leaves the call in.

chapterSummaries: Rusk slid his lamp-less barge alongside, gave Sol until the storm turns to hand over the cold-case's value or the Marrow itself, pocketed three of Teo's four medicine cartridges as "earnest," and cast off east—leaving behind word of a sealed pharmacy pocket at forty-two meters in Mercy General that no diver has ever come back from, the same depth where a man everyone says is dead keeps calling Wren's name on the backup channel. Wren, who rebuilds divers' lost hours from the data their body kept, understands she has never once built her own.

Wren built her own slate and found an eleven-second cut matching the one she'd made in Sol's — then found fifty-two minutes erased from her own deck log and every redundant record aboard, all sealed by a hand that knew her method too well: her own. Before anyone could stop him, Dey rolled off the rail with no rig, no clip, no line, one breath, stroking west toward Mercy General. The storm hit the Marrow broadside, the deck heeled, and Dey went under.

chapter.title: Below the Line
beats: In the storm's first hard blow, Nia and Sol get the loose line and a boat-hook out to Dey and drag him to the rail; he comes over the side alive but wrong — lips gray, eyes not tracking, too heavy and too quiet.

Working him on the deck, Wren reads Dey's slate fast and finds the last hour gone as a soft, water-made dropout, not a cut — the deep ate it below the line, and Dey surfaces with no memory of the tower or the pocket he swam for.

With no rig sealing past thirty and only Wren's own suit rated to forty-two, and her voice still on last night's comms saying "at pocket, seal intact," Wren is the only one who can find the pharmacy pocket — and she says yes to going back down into the same dark she erased.

Sol takes the winch instead of the water, planting herself at the drum and feeding Wren the boat's last good air down the spliced line, spending the drum's single remaining pull as Wren's only ride up.

Wren goes down the spliced line alone, Sol calling the meters as the storm hammers the hull, the rule of the deep made real when Wren passes thirty and the cold starts working at the edge of her thinking.

At forty-two meters her lamp finds the sealed pharmacy pocket — and tied at the seal is her own knot from last night, the one she doesn't remember tying, her hands already knowing it before her mind catches up.
events: Nia and Sol haul Dey aboard alive but unresponsive — gray-lipped, eyes fixed, body heavy with the deep — while Wren freezes at the winch and Sol demands she read his slate.

Wren reads Dey's slate, confirms the deep ate his last fifty-one minutes rather than anyone cutting them, and proves no seam exists anywhere aboard — then Dey speaks her name as the backup channel speaks it too.

Wren plays last night's comms and hears her own voice at the sealed pocket swearing to bring the winch — a descent she has no memory of — realizes her suit is the only one aboard rated to forty-two meters, and suits up to dive back into the dark she erased.
Sol takes the winch position, rigs the last air bottle to the spliced line, and commits the drum's single remaining pull as Wren's only ride up, sending Wren down into the storm-lashed water.

Wren passes thirty meters and starts losing her thinking in real time, and Salas answers her hail two-way to explain that she gave him her name last night and told him to say it first if she came back not knowing it — while her slate shows twenty-two minutes elapsed for a dive she only remembers nine of.
